prompts.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: full-screen 16:9 illustrated memory cinematic for a darkly funny office action game. Create exactly ONE continuous landscape illustration, no panels. Artistic medium: expressive graphite outlines, translucent watercolor and gouache, luminous muted amber and blue with selective vibrant accents, paper grain, unfinished sketch edges, tender lived-in human acting, visually sophisticated storybook graphic novel, no artist imitation. This is a remembered shared moment, slightly dreamlike, emotionally sincere with one small office absurdity. The engineer is ALWAYS a tired Filipino man in his early thirties, medium-brown skin, messy short black hair, faint stubble, charcoal rolled-sleeve shirt, dark blue trousers, an office lanyard, tired kind eyes. Make people anatomically convincing with expressive gestures, no toy or chibi bodies. Keep narrative action within the upper 75 percent; lower 20 percent is quiet painterly space for in-game subtitles. No title, speech bubbles, UI, watermark or captions. Background people, if present, are doing relevant work, never aimlessly wandering. Memory: Morgan, a fair-skinned blond manager in a loosened navy suit, secretly holds an elevator open with his foot while balancing two takeaway coffees. He reaches one coffee toward the exhausted engineer who is mid-step escaping the office, his shoulders relaxing into a rare grin. Their hands meet around the cup. View from inside an amber elevator toward a cool fluorescent office corridor; company papers and inboxes recede out of focus. Elevator doors framing this small conspiracy, glowing Friday evening outside glass. Cinematic intimate wide shot with diagonal motion and warm negative space. A tiny coffee receipt is tucked in Morgan's folder as if it were a leadership document. Capture friendship through an action, not two stationary people talking.

Close low cinematic composition concentrating on linked fingers and the optimistic young face. Amber and dusty coral, poignant unfinished promise. Do not depict them already eating noodles: the lunch has yet to happen.
